segment.source:
::You walk toward the buff barkeeper, but somewhere along the way a mug flies before your eyes, from left to right, and collides with some poor squeezer's head. The blow sends the fellow to the floor, face first, while everybody around him laughs at his misfortune, including the barkeeper. You finally approach him, and he yells at you, as that seems to be the only way to be heard in this place.::
Welcome to Hardcore City Bar, the place where the most hardcore meet to have a drink! I haven't seen $(#you/your pretty face) before. I'm Gene, the owner, and this here is my beautiful wife Harriette. Name your poison, $(#mate/love).<end>
<end>
Let's see what you got. ::Barter.::<end>
I need to talk to Gorsky.<end>
::He leans forward and speaks in a whisper.:: Absolutely. Take this key here and use the back entrance. It's just around the corner. Out and around the corner to the north.<end>
::He winks, then laughs and continues talking loudly.:: That's a good joke! Very funny!<end>
What do you know about the Black Sea?<end>
I know as much as everyone else. Pirates, serpents, mysterious stuff... ooohh.<end>

I figure, if you really wanna learn more about it, go talk to the ferrymen. Yeah, I know, I know, they like colorin' their stories with all kinds of hardcore superstitions, but there's a lot of truth to what they say. That's my advice to you, $(#mate/love).<end>
Have you heard of Aegis Incorporated?<end>
Absolutely, $(#mate/love). Ever since they showed up at the docks everyone's been asking about them. <end>

They are one of the largest private security companies from North Underrail and have been around for quite a few years. Actually, I was once considering hiring them to protect my wife while we were on a trip to North Underrail. I reckon, when them Northern wimps see one of our beautiful Southern girls...<end>
Oh, stop, you.<end>
::He smiles.:: Anyways, the Aegis guys mean hardcore business, and they have a dominating record so--<end>
I didn't mean you should actually stop, Gene. I just said it.<end>
Oh. Yeah.<end>
Why do Northerners need a security company when they have Underrail Protectorate?<end>

Well, they need someone to protect them when they come here. You know how dangerous this place is, and not just 'cause of local gangs and such, but Free Drones too. They like taking hostages and exchanging them for their own captured comrades. Protectorate can't babysit everyone, so the wealthy merchants and fat rats hire these security companies to escort them.<end>

Even though there's a lot more Protectorate in the South, these folks still need private security. Now, what's currently going on is that they've been hired for some kind of an expedition to the Black Sea, so they brought pretty much everything they got, $(#mate/love). That's hardcore business.<end>
Let's change the subject.<end>
Sure thing, $(#mate/love).<end>
I'm looking for some information on Spectres, a former Biocorp special forces unit. Do you know anything about them?<end>
Hmmm... That sounds familiar, $(#mate/love).... Spectres... Spectres...<end>
Ah, I remember now, I think, I think Oskar talked about that a few years ago. Absolutely, I remember it now!<end>
Why would Oskar know anything about Spectres?<end>
I don't know, he was an enforcer in Praetorian Security before he opened his store. Maybe it had something to do with his job, I don't know $(#mate/love).<end>
Maybe he can help you with these Spectres you're asking about.<end>
Who's Oskar?<end>
He's the owner of Oskar's Armory. His store is just outside the bar, $(#mate/love).<end>
Why would he know anything about Spectres?<end>
I need some information on a former Praetorian Security officer called Patrick Pierce.<end>
Never heard of him, $(#mate/love).<end>
Maybe Praetorian Security is a good place to ask?<end>
I'm here to ask for your help with Daniel Arda.<end>
Absolutely! Anything you need.<end>
I have evidence that proves Hercules is an extremely dangerous substance. I just need to somehow present it to everyone in Core City.<end>

So you came to me, $(#mate/love)? I'm glad for it, because I know just the right man for the job. This guy can access one of those Gauntlet ad displays, and he can put on view whatever you want. He already did it before, but that's a different story that began with some heavy intoxication. ::He laughs.:: Just give me the evidence and I'll take care of everything.<end>
You really hate him, don't you. ::Give him the flash drive.::<end>

Nope. ::He laughs.:: I've got nothing against that cyclops, I don't know what you're talking about.
So, everything's here... You just wait a while and everyone will know. Absolutely everyone!<end>
<end>
Here you go. ::Give him the flash drive.::<end>
Thanks $(#mate/love). So, everything's here... You just wait a while and everyone will know. Absolutely everyone!<end>
Maybe it's better that I do it myself. How can I gain access to the advertisement display?<end>

If I remember correctly, the easiest one to access is right near the lower level elevator. There's a way to access the terminal there, underneath the display, but I haven't done that myself so I can't give you any more details, $(#mate/love).<end>
I changed my mind, I'll let your guy upload the Hercules evidence.<end>
Sure, no problem $(#mate/love). Just let me have it and I'll take care of the rest<end>
On a second thought, nothing yet. Let's discuss something else.<end>
Oh... Yeah, go ahead.<end>
I need some general directions.<end>

Absolutely. Core City is quite simple to understand $(#mate/love). You are currently on the middle level of Core City. You've got your merchants here as well as the Arena, just west from the bar. The whole eastern area of this level is Drop Zone; avoid it if possible.<end>

Above us is the residential area. There you'll find Coretech, Praetorian Security and JKK buildings, three major enterprises of Core City.
Above that is the entrance, or exit, however you see it, to Upper Underrail.<end>

Below us is the lower level, which has the main entrance, and below that, docks. Sewers also, but you absolutely don't want to go there. Also, the lower level can be accessed through the under-passages, but people rarely go there 'cause of the Lurkers, you know about that.
As I said, Core City is quite easy to navigate, $(#mate/love). ::He laughs.::<end>
What can you tell me about the Talloski family?<end>

Oooh, the Talloskies are hardcore players here in Core City. Absolutely, $(#mate/love). You don't want to be messing around with them. ::He leans toward you and whispers.:: The head of the family, Vlatko, has earned himself serious connections with Chief Knight of Praetorian Security. I know him personally, and let me tell you, the man is a successful businessman.<end>
His daughter, Sophie, comes here from time to time. She seems like a really spoiled brat to me.<end>
Harriette! Don't let anyone hear you say that! Shush, my love!<end>
I'd like to ask you about certain people here in Core City.<end>
Absolutely. Who are we talking about here?<end>
Merchants.<end>
Say the name and I'll deliver.<end>
<end>
Al Fabet.<end>

Not him, just not him! He's absolutely derailed. I mean, he, he comes here from time to time and puts some stinkin' animal hearts on the table. I tell him to get lost, he tells me - and you're not gonna believe this - he tells me: "What the hell! Barkeepers are merchants. They should be able to buy what I offer them, like, yeah. So, how much will you give me for these hearts?"<end>
Calm down, Gene. He hasn't shown up ever since you punched him in the nose.<end>
::He laughs.:: He comes back sometimes, sits outside. Gives me collywobbles when I see him. Ugh.<end>
Jon the Beautiful.<end>

He's a nice kid, a bit odd with his food-for-information policy, but it's been working out for him, which is hardcore. You can find him behind the bar most of the time... That's where he hangs out when he's not at Moe's stall.<end>
And he is also very cute.<end>
What? So when I tell a girl she's got a nice patootie, you slam me over the head with a pan, but when you say someone's cute, it's okay?<end>
Shut up, sweetie.<end>
Ladelman.<end>
Tone! Tony Ladelman. Why, he used to work here as a bouncer.<end>
No one could make me laugh as hard as him, I swear. It's that checking-the-pipes kind of laughter, you dig.<end>

He's a great guy to be around. And knew everything. It's 'cause he used to do all kinds of jobs before he started working for me: quad mechanic, construction worker, weaponsmith, electrician, bodyguard, scrap assembler...<end>
Train operator.<end>
Ferryman, ferry mechanic...<end>
Railkill collector.<end>
Sewer inspector...<end>
Mh... art model.<end>
You name it, he's done it. Girls included, ha. ::He shyly glances at Harriette.:: Uh, too bad he had to quit this job. He punched a guest, almost zoned him out cold.<end>
Isn't that what bouncers are supposed to do?<end>

Yeah. But that time the guest was Maxim Talloski, son of one of the wealthiest people in Core City. You dig. So Tone had to lay low for a while after that, and returning to working as a bouncer was simply out of the question.
Kind of lost touch with him after that.<end>
I miss him. Remember that funny story he used to tell about his sister Lilly? About how she had to bite off that guy's... You know the story I'm talking about, Gene?<end>
Nnnnot really, no. Actually, I... don't know anything about his sister, love. No.<end>
Who's the black guy with the fissure tattoo?<end>
The guy over there? That's Gorge, at least that's how I heard some people call him. He's not a talkative fellow, $(#mate/love). <end>
He's an Underrail Express train operator and one of the more frequent patrons. Just comes here, orders drinks, dominates a few bottles all by himself, then leaves.<end>
He also seems prone to fistfights.<end>
Really now, love, that only happened once! And he was provoked.<end>

Some pipeworker - a zoner, completely unimportant - was bugging him about something. Gorge got up and hit him right in the middle of his face, sending teeth all across the bar. One gal immediately yelled, "Hey, I wanted ice in my drink - not teeth!" to which we all laughed.<end>
While the zoner was choking on one of his own.<end>
Well, I never wanted him to choke on it in my bar - so I threw him out.<end>
You mess with my patrons, you better drop off. Right, $(#mate/love)?<end>
Do you know anything about his tattooed scar?<end>

I've heard rumors, $(#mate/love). Some say his father did it to him when he was young, as a punishment. Other's say he got it in a fight when he was protecting his brother from bandits. His brother got killed, and Gorge passed out from blood loss, after killing every pipeworker there. He would've died if someone hadn't found him.<end>
That's what I've heard, but how true it is... I don't know.<end>
I'd like to ask you about someone else.<end>
Yes?<end>
I had other questions for you.<end>
I'm listening.<end>
Gorge.<end>
Mac, the graffiti artist.<end>

Absolutely, $(#mate/love)! You've probably seen a lot of graffiti around the city. Most of those were done by Mac himself. I can't tell you a lot about him; he comes here occasionally, but he keeps to himself most of the time.<end>
He brings in a lot of girls to the bar. Very *attractive* girls.<end>
I don't know how and where he picks them up, but he's good at it! ::He sighs.:: He's so damn hardcore.<end>
Why is he hardcore? He can't be loyal to a single woman so he changes them like socks. Nothing hardcore about it.<end>
Um... Yes, love! You are absolutely right! A man should be loyal to a single woman and not even think about other women ever again.<end>
I'd like to ask about someone else.<end>
<end>
Professor Norman Hack.<end>
Norman Hack. Do you know what that imbecile did? He came to the bar and spoke in his... advantalk, advatale, whatever. Obviously no one understands him, because he made it up...<end>
Northerners...<end>
Then he makes a fuss about it, complains that we're uneducated and tells us he's not coming back until we learn... that language he made up.<end>
Northerners...<end>
You're right, love. Northerners...<end>
Do you know anything about that young, well-dressed fellow who's sitting upstairs?<end>
Oh, you mean Mr. Handsome.<end>
It's that spruce man who flirts with me every time he comes here, and every time he does that I can feel you sulking somewhere in the background.<end>
Mr. *Pipeworker*, more like it. There's something off about that guy, something hardcore off. Don't like him one bit.<end>
You're just jealous, dear.<end>

Well, I don't like pipeworkers hitting on my beautiful... perfect wife. But he ain't right, you know. He looks right, but he ain't. He's some kinda weird psionic, I hear. Some... time ma-- Temporal Manipulation thing, yes. Don't like him one bit.<end>
He's got style, nonetheless. Dominating style.<end>
Ethan Lanford.<end>
Yeah... how about you pick another name, $(#mate/love).<end>
The psiworking bastard...<end>
<end>
Mykola.<end>

Mykola Young? He owns the mechanics store near Halim's electronics. Um, I mean, *owned* the store. It's closed now, as the poor guy got into some problems with... ::He whispers.:: the Oligarchs. No one I talked to knows what *exactly* happened, but it's no secret that Mykola opposed the way the Oligarchs rule Core City. He wasn't exactly subtle about it either. Especially not when his daughter started working for JKK. You can imagine how he felt about that, $(#mate/love).
In the end, maybe all that finally got him into trouble. ::He shrugs.:: Or it could be something else. Who knows. <end>

Regardless, he got really ill following the recent events; his coughing is so nasty it makes you appreciate the tranquil sounds of trains braking.
Poor guy got dominated by life.<end>
Sergio.<end>
Listen carefuly, Sergio is your man if you want to... You know. ::He whispers.:: Get into Motion.<end>
Gene, why are you whispering? Everyone here knows abou--<end>
My dear love, that might be correct, but still...<end>
Just go see him. ::He winks.::<end>
Oskar, the weapons store owner.<end>
Oskar! Oskar - he's the most hardcore patron I've ever had. I love that man, absolutely the best.<end>
I never liked Oskar, he always seems so full of himself. He used to be a Praetorian enforcer. So what? But I still smile when he says hi. It's common courtesy.<end>
That's enough, love. I love you, but please...<end>
Derica, the general store owner.<end>

Now that woman is gorgeous. She's funny, she's smart, she runs a successful business... What more can a guy ask for, right?
$(#She's married, mate. Just so you know./)<end>
Indeed...<end>
::Gene remains quiet.::<end>
Dr. Heidi Gratz.<end>
Glad you asked me, $(#mate/love). I often get asked how come such a derailed person can be such a good doctor? I tell them this:<end>

She is the best doctor I've ever had the pleasure of being cut open by. Heidi has had a traumatic experience in the past, as she had to do an emergency operation on her husband. He died on the table. Poor woman crossed the tracks.<end>
It's a tragedy...<end>
Halim, the electronics merchant.<end>

He's a... different person than the rest of us. I never see him at the bar, he doesn't like going to the Arena... He is an expert in what he does, but I'll be damned, $(#mate/love), he's strange.<end>
I like him, he's quiet. And an intellectual. Those Tchortists also <end>
seemed pretty intellectual, if you ask me.<end>
Good riddance. The smartest things those people did was pack their bags and leave.<end>
seem pretty intellectual, if you ask me.<end>
Don't let them hear you, love - they'll come swarming in. They'll drive all the patrons away!<end>
Moe.<end>
Moe's a dear friend of ours. What can I say, he is one hard-working, honest and good-looking man. Some have also mentioned he and I look alike! Isn't that funny?<end>

You'll find him near the entrance to the city, on the lower level. He's got a hardcore food stall there, just by the elevator. And the food is just... absolutely splendid. Try it out sometimes, $(#mate/love)! Just do it. ::He laughs.::<end>
Zilla.<end>
Zilla? Oooh, she's a bomb, $(#mate/love)!<end>
Excuse me!?<end>
No, love, I didn't mean it like *that*! I meant that she... uh, she has an explosive personality. Absolutely! You know Zilla.<end>

Nevertheless, let me explain: In most cases, Zilla is a very nice and friendly person. In most cases... Yet, if something doesn't go her way she becomes this hardcore anger-machine. I mean, we all saw what happened between Moe and her...<end>
Not all of us.<end>

Well, some time ago both Moe and her had a food stall at the lower level city entrance. Let's face it, $(#mate/love), the Lower Underrail station has more traffic than the Upper Underrail one. You've got people from the North, people from all the southern stations, Junkyard... A dominating position. <end>

Zilla was angry that Moe's business was more hardcore than hers, so one day she went berserk and accused Moe of "stealing" her business and, listen to this - she even kicked his stall and threw his food all over the place. It was hardcore!<end>
She's up there now, at the Upper Underrail station... She's behaving for the time being, as far as I know. But the point of the story is - she's a bit derailed! That's it, $(#mate/love).<end>
What happened between Moe and her?<end>
Ray Cerr.<end>

Ray. ::He shakes his head.:: Hope they catch the burglar scum.
Now, about Ray, he's <end>
one of my most hardcore patrons, I gotta say.<end>
I've always "liked" the way he puts his dirty tools on my counter.<end>
Come on, love, where else is he gonna put them?<end>
Toolbox. Bag. Pocket. Floor. Outside.<end>
You're overreacting, love. It's nothing a simple cloth can't clean.<end>

Anyways, he's the only proper jet ski dealer in South Underrail. Ever since he bought the premises at the docks his business started booming. Nowadays you can see all kinds of dominating jets at his store.<end>
He's an honest man who'd never, and I mean it, never ever rip anyone off. If he ain't got what you need - no one got it. The prices are fair and the service is hardcore. <end>
::He shakes his head again.:: Bloody thieving scum, why must they always target the good folks...<end>
<end>
Way to advertise your friend.<end>
He does it whenever he gets the chance.<end>
Love!<end>
Let me ask you about someone else.<end>
Just say the name, $(#mate/love).<end>
Oh, Ray. Why, he's <end>
Rag.<end>
Rag, Rag, Rag... The clothing zoner, right?<end>
I went to his place once.<end>

You we-- What!? Of all the hardcore shops in Core City *proper* you chose to go to literal Pipeworks?
You could've been dominated there!<end>

Oh, shut up, dear. It's close by, and besides, everyone knows whose wife I am.
I'm not going back there anyway: The place is filthy, the owner is rude, and the only shirt I liked had a bullet hole straight through the middle, both front and back.<end>

Women. The things they'd do for cheaper rags.
Well, I guess you heard all you needed to know, $(#mate/love).<end>
Non-residents.<end>
Regular folks. If regular is the right word.<end>
Changed my mind. There's something more important.<end>
Do you know anything about a merchant named Daniel Arda?<end>
Oh, the cyclops... I know him, and I dislike him, $(#mate/love). He comes here often, pretending to be hardcore, orders a drink and then blatantly hits on my wife before these two eyes!<end>
What about the time you were hitting on Derica when she was here with her husband?<end>

I wasn't hitting on her, love, I was just being friendly! You know I would never hit on another woman!
Nevertheless, where were we... The cyclops. I think he's doing some really *questionable* business. That Hercules thing sounds like a hoax if I've ever seen one. I've heard of some men who bought it, left Core City and never came back.<end>
Look, if you need any *help* with that guy, let me know. ::He winks.:: No one hits on my wife!<end>
Ever heard of Joe De Pacino?<end>
I don't think I have. I know a lot of people in Core City, but a De Pacino...<end>
Sorry, but no. Can't remember anyone that goes by that name.<end>
::[Persuade]:: Yes, you do and you're going to tell me where to find him.<end>

::His answer does not come quickly; he carefully looks around before eventually replying in a quiet voice.::
Look, I can't talk about him.<end>
Why not?<end>
He doesn't like when people talk about him. And if he finds out...<end>
He's one hardcore fellow. And he's got big players backing him up from what I've heard.<end>
So do I. And who are these players?<end>
Some say Protectorate, some say Coretech. I don't know, but I do know that Joe De Pacino is a serious player.<end>
Tell me where to find him.<end>
::He remains silent, looking around the bar.::<end>
He won't find out you told me about him.<end>
Go north until you get to a small shack overlooking the chasm. That's the place. There's a guard there.<end>
::He suddenly raises his voice.:: So, one coal train was it? Absolutely! Coming right up, $(#mate/love).<end>
Praetorian Security want's him gone. Just tell me where he is and that's problem solved for us all.<end>
Spill it. There's no backing away now.<end>
You're scared of him?<end>
No. Yes. You know.<end>
No, I don't. I already told you. Please, stop asking me about him.<end>
Now, what can I get you, $(#mate/love)?<end>
Fine. Let me ask you about something else.<end>
Ever heard of Bogdan Stravohodnik?<end>
He's on the black list, $(#mate/love). I've seen him only once, and that's enough for a lifetime.<end>
Can you tell me what happened?<end>

A squabble! He came here, angry, derailed or whatever, and grabbed a guy called Slavomir. Slavomir is a regular patron here, a funny and good-natured zoner, and from what I heard during the fighting, the two are brothers.<end>
Then what happened?<end>
I mean, a lot of those zoners tend to cause trouble, but Slavomir, now he was the opposite. He was so--<end>
Gene, just answer the $(#gentleman/lady) already...<end>
Oh, right! Well, they got into a fight. These things happen, and are often welcome entertainment, but this Bogdan threw a bottle and damaged my monitor. So I threw them both outta here.<end>
Where did they go to after you threw them out?<end>
I don't know. All I know is that as they were duking it out one of them dropped this key, which I picked up later while cleaning the place.<end>
What Gene meant sweetie, is that *I* found the key when *I* did the cleaning, because cleaning is beneath him.<end>
Uh... It's not like that... I mean... Never mind, just take this. ::He gives you a small key.::<end>
Do you know where I might start searching for the two?<end>
Drop Zone. Makes absolute sense, eh, $(#mate/love)?<end>
Okay, thanks. Goodbye.<end>
I'm listening.<end>
How do you feel about the Faceless invasion?<end>
If they do break into the city, I'll give them free drinks. ::He laughs.::<end>
What Gene wanted to say is, he'd start quaking before the Faceless and try to bribe them with booze.<end>
Why, love? Why?<end>
Sweetie, I'm joking. Hardcore men know how to take a joke. And cook, clean, tell their wives they love them from time to time and have the... ::She clears her throat.::<end>
What can you tell me about your wife?<end>
Absolutely. She's gorgeous, wonderful, smart, funny. This bar would feel so empty and lifeless without her and, and...<end>
That's enough, Gene, I can see you've practiced. And you haven't complimented a girl's patootie in days. I love you. ::She smiles.::<end>
Dominating!<end>
I'm looking for the Acid Hunters.<end>
Mmmm, I know them. They're led by this guy... Hmmm...<end>
Cornell.<end>
Cornell! The green mohawk guy. Thanks, love.<end>

A bunch of scavengers. They come here from time to time. Can't tell you much else about them, really.
Haven't seen them in a while... Who knows, maybe they're dead. ::He laughs.::<end>
I'm looking for Terry and Lora Baker. They are merchants from South Gate Station. Have you seen them perhaps?<end>
Absolutely. I know the two. They've visited the bar numerous times. The problem is, I can't exactly remember when was the last time they were here...<end>
Around the time the big earthquake happened?<end>

::He takes a moment to think.:: Yes, that's right. The earthquake stopped all Underrail Express traffic and many were unable to leave the city. The bar was packed back then - not that I'm complaining, $(#mate/love). It was hardcore. Nevertheless, I remember seeing them at the bar during that time. ::He turns to Harriette.:: Right, love?<end>
Mmm, what? Oh, the Bakers? Yes, yes. They were here at the time.<end>
There you go.<end>
Anything else you can tell me?<end>
No. That's pretty much all of it.<end>
Right. Thanks for the info. I've got more questions for you, if I may ask them?<end>
::He nods.:: Absolutely, $(#mate/love).<end>
Bye.<end>
What in dominating hell happened up there? The patrons told me you got attacked by that psionic, Ethan.<end>
<end>
Praetorian Security business.<end>
Oh. Well then... For the record, <end>
Never trusted that guy. I knew he ain't right. I knew it.<end>
Now do you believe me?<end>
I-- But-- He was Mr. Handsome!<end>
Well... now he's Mr. *Deadsome*.<end>
So?<end>

So...
Care for a drink, $(#mate/love)?<end>
What happens now?<end>
Nothing. Nothing happens. Just keep it quiet and everything's gonna be hardcore. Dig?<end>
Coretech business.<end>
JKK business.<end>
That son of a rat was completely derailed! I don't know what came over him. He just attacked me.<end>
::He slowly nods a few times.:: <end>
We got into an argument. He attacked me. Now he's dead. That's it.<end>
That's between me and him.<end>
Hey, this is my bar! If I ask you a question I wanna hear an answer.<end>
::He laughs.:: The cyclops is finally gone.<end>
$(#Mate/Love)! Good to see you. Since the Faceless have *sadly* departed, every patron gets a drink on the house. Here's yours. Dominate it! ::He hands you a mushroom brew.::<end>
Caught the news on Edmund Knight, $(#mate/love)? He got zoned out good, but there's something fishy in that whole story. If you got any info, do share.<end>
<end>

Hey, know anything about a $(context.npc_cc_ray_describeBreakIn_finalDescription)? Someone broke into Ray's shop at the docks, and the Praetorians think this person did it. Just so you know, $(#mate/love).<end>
You heard about the Talloski murders? If someone could dominate one of the most protected families in the city... ::He shakes his head.::<end>
Hey, love, can I help you with something? ::He winks.::<end>
What can I get you, mate?<end>
